summary: SNAT port overcommit during nightly prefetch jobs causes intermittent presigned range 403s
description:
Issue summary: During the customer's nightly prefetch/concurrency job, a subset of multipart range GETs for presigned model shard downloads fail with HTTP 403. Impact: client-side ingestion pipeline reports intermittent 403s causing retry storms and falling behind nightly prefetch SLA. Behavior is sporadic (not all shards) and correlates with the nightly job window.

Observed at Redwood edge: signature mismatch for presigned requests where requests appear to originate from different source IPs or port translations mid-download. Customer uses IP-restricted presigned URLs (security policy) which make them sensitive to SNAT/EIP mapping changes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer runs nightly prefetch: 120 parallel workers fetch model shards via presigned range GETs using IP-restricted presigned URLs.
2) Observe ~1-5% of range requests return 403 in server logs during peak concurrency window (00:15–00:45 UTC).
3) Re-running same concurrent load outside nightly window does not reproduce unless SNAT allocation is constrained on customer side.
4) Reducing concurrency to 20 workers removes 403s reproducibly; increasing concurrency reproduces failure rate.
5) Curl sample against presigned range shows 403 with server-side log entry indicating 'signature does not match signed host/IP'.
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): verified 403s are not coming from Redwood ACLs; server validates presigned token and checks allowed source IP list attached at presign time.
Correlation: 403s spike only during customer's nightly prefetch window and only when the job uses high concurrency and reuses a small number of outbound EIPs/EIPs-per-NAT configuration.

Hypothesis: customer NAT device/nat-gateway ran short on ephemeral port/NAT translations, causing source IP/EIP or port to change mid-stream (or between range requests) and some requests observed from an EIP not present in the presigned allowlist -> 403.
Evidence: customer provided VPC flow logs showing different public EIP on near-simultaneous chunk requests for the same logical worker; conntrack reported exhaustion spikes during failures.
Edge/server logs show a consistent pattern: failing requests have eip not listed in the presigned token metadata; succeeding requests show allowed eip.
We reproduced locally by constraining outbound EIP pool and running 120 parallel range GETs against IP-restricted presigned URLs -> reproducible 403 rate ~2-4%.
comments: Customer (Kenji Tanaka) - 2026-03-10: 'We saw about 300 failing shard downloads during our nightly run. Our security team requires presigned URLs to be IP-locked.'
Support (Aisha): 'Thanks Kenji — we will correlate edge logs and reproduce. Can you provide conntrack metrics and number of EIPs attached to your NAT? Also, do you rotate EIPs via autoscaling?'
Customer (Kenji) - 2026-03-10: 'We're using a single NAT appliance with 2 EIPs and 120 concurrent workers. Conntrack peaked at 65535 during the window.'

SRE (Diego Morales) - 2026-03-11: 'Reproduced in lab by limiting EIP count and forcing high concurrency; failures map to NAT port exhaustion and EIP reassign behavior. Proposed workaround: throttle concurrency or add EIP/Egress capacity.'
Support (Aisha) - 2026-03-11: 'Provided workaround steps + recommended permanent mitigations. Customer applied temporary throttle and reported immediate reduction in failures.'
Customer (Kenji) - 2026-03-12: 'After throttling and adding 3 more EIPs to NAT pool, 403s disappeared in two nightly runs. We'll follow up to make the change permanent.'
resolution_notes: Workaround applied by customer: reduced concurrency from 120 -> 24 workers for nightly prefetch; immediately removed 403s.
Permanent fix: customer provisioned 3 additional EIPs on their NAT instance and increased conntrack and ephemeral port range. Post-change verification across two nightly runs shows 0 failures.

Platform guidance provided: avoid IP-restricted presigned URLs if prefetch uses large-scale ephemeral concurrency; instead use signed URLs with short TTL and authentication at application layer OR provision sufficient egress EIP capacity and monitor conntrack metrics.

Follow-up action (internal): create INT ticket to add an entry in Private Deploy networking runbook about 'prefetch concurrency and SNAT sizing' and a diagnostic playbook for presigned-403 debugging. Linked INT ticket created (INT-4512).
